subject: Private evidence onboarding for VPC observability — playbook and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Laura Matthews <laura.m@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Private evidence onboarding for VPC observability — playbook and next steps

Morning Laura —

Thanks again for agreeing to run the private observability onboarding with Acme. To keep this lightweight and auditable, I've sketched a short playbook for the evidence we typically need when customers host telemetry in a VPC/on-prem forwarder pattern. Attachments: evidence_manifest_v1.csv (list of common items), network_topology_vpc.pdf (placeholder).

Top asks to unblock the engineering onboarding: 
- Confirm SIEM receiver details (Splunk HEC endpoint, port, token rotation cadence).
- Egress constraints: whether the forwarder can reach redwood-egress.redwood.com or must go via an approved NAT/proxy (and IP allowlist).
- Retention and custody: any data residency or retention windows we should be aware of (logs/traces/metrics).
- TLS requirements: mTLS required? custom CA?

Can you reply with the above (or point me at the right contact)? If easier, let's set a 30m sync this week. Proposed owners: Acme security for SIEM details, Acme infra for topology, Kimberly for telemetry mapping, Marcus for runbook provisioning.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence_manifest_v1.csv (type: csv, stub), network_topology_vpc.pdf (type: pdf, stub)

From: Laura Matthews <laura.m@acmehealth.com>

Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Private evidence onboarding for VPC observability — playbook and next steps

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and attached a sanitized topology export.

- SIEM: We use Splunk HEC (https://splunk.acmehealth.com:8088/services/collector). We'll share a short-lived HEC token via your secure link. No changes to port.
- Egress: All outbound must go through our egress gateway at 35.201.12.24; only allowlisted destinations are permitted. We cannot open arbitrary outbound to external IPs.
- Retention: Logs 13 months, traces 90 days, metrics 24 months (aggregated).
- TLS: mTLS is preferred for log ingestion. We manage our own CA; we can provide a cert bundle or accept Redwood's certificate if you support CA pinning.

Procurement note: procurement@acmehealth.com says they'll need a short SOC2 evidence bundle before provisioning tokens. I'll attach an initial evidence checklist (redacted).

Laura
Laura Matthews
Director, Security Operations — Acme Health
---
Attachments: network_topology_vpc_acme_redacted.pdf (type: pdf, stub), acme_evidence_checklist.xlsx (type: xlsx, stub)

Thanks Laura — couple of clarifying technical Qs from the engineering side: 

- For Splunk HEC behind the egress gateway: will Acme provide NAT IP translation or do we need to deploy an outbound proxy appliance inside the VPC? If proxy, what auth method is required?
- mTLS: can you share the CA bundle and CRL/OCSP expectations? Do certs rotate automatically (short-lived) or are they long-lived?
- Tracing hooks: we plan to add a small trace context header (x-redwood-trace) on forwarded requests — does Acme want that preserved and mapped in Splunk? If so, specify the field name
- Mapping: we'll provide a starter Splunk HEC payload mapping and sample events. If you can confirm event field names for user_id, tenant_id, and request_id we can align.

I've attached a short handshake checklist (handshake_checklist.xlsx) and a stub of our Splunk mapping. Next step from my side is a runbook draft for a customer-side forwarder deployment (stepwise, ephemeral provisioning, service account rotation).

Adding a couple engineering notes and I can own the runbook delivery: 

- We will provide two options for Acme depending on egress policy: (A) lightweight in-VPC ephemeral forwarder (containerized, runs in customer subnet, rolls credentials via KMS/HSM) or (B) managed outbound proxy that Acme allows to talk to our egress gateway (IP allowlist).
- For Splunk HEC + mTLS: we'll support Acme CA bundle; forwarder will present client cert signed by Redwood's intermediate during onboarding if Acme prefers that flow. We'll add OCSP checks in the runbook.
- Trace propagation: we will preserve x-redwood-trace and map it to splunk field rw_trace_id; request_id -> request_id, tenant_id -> tenant_id.
- Audit & evidence: we'll include a minimal evidence packet (sha256 checksums, manifest CSV, and runbook snapshot) to satisfy procurement and SOC2 reviewers.

I'll post the runbook draft by Fri Oct 8 EOD (internal review beforehand). Scheduling: Tue Oct 12 10:00am ET works for me.

Marcus Lin
